result.question: Discuss the major types of unemployment prevalent in India. What measures can address them? (Answer in 250 words)

directives.meaning: Look at the issue from more than one side, with reasons, and reach a balanced view.

sentences.text: Unemployment refers to a situation in which people who are willing and able to work at prevailing wages cannot find work.
In India it appears more often as underemployment and low-quality work than as open joblessness.
Open unemployment exists when people actively seek work but find none, a pattern more visible in urban areas.
Disguised unemployment occurs when more people are engaged in a task than needed, so that withdrawing some would not reduce output.
It is common in Indian agriculture, where family members share work on small farms.
Seasonal unemployment arises because farm work is available only in certain months of the year.
Structural unemployment results from a mismatch between the skills of workers and the jobs available, or from inadequate productive capacity.
Educated unemployment is widespread among youth whose qualifications do not match labour market needs.
Many workers are pushed into the informal sector, where they lack regular income and social security.
Over the decades, workers have also moved from self-employment and regular salaried jobs to casual wage work, a process called casualisation.
Since 2019, labour force surveys have been conducted by the National Statistical Office, formed by merging the NSSO and the CSO.
Measures include promoting labour-intensive manufacturing and MSMEs, expanding skill development, encouraging rural non-farm employment and extending social security to informal workers.
Public works such as those under the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act, 2005 provided a safety net for rural households.
Sustained job-rich growth, rather than growth alone, is essential for India to reap its demographic dividend.
